audit_findings.title: Federal coal-lease purchase obligations are omitted from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $33.489 million present value, equal to $0.63 per diluted share and 1.24% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds cash and short-term investments but does not deduct the separately recorded federal coal-lease acquisition obligations; these installments are not captured by retaining ordinary interest expense in equity-level OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company bid approximately $ 46.8 million for the Leases and has submitted a payment for approximately $ 9.4 million, which is the first of five equal installments.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge omission: the June 2026 filing records $9.100 million current and $24.389 million long-term obligations, while the stated bridge contains neither. Nevertheless, a full $33.489 million deduction would reduce base value from $50.50 to about $49.87 per share and would not change the conclusion relative to the $104.45 market price.
audit_findings.action: Rerun the bridge with a $33.489 million deduction unless the model can document that all remaining installments are already included in forecast OE.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 sustaining capital is not representative of the enlarged operating base
audit_findings.magnitude: $43.7-$53.7 million annual sustaining-capital shortfall versus FY2025, equal to 25.9%-31.9% of the $168.6 million anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Maintenance capital is deducted in OE; using FY2025 sustaining capital of $61.3 million instead of the filed 2026 requirement of $105-$115 million inflates the recurring OE anchor and every forecast period derived from it.
audit_findings.evidence: Our capital spending is expected to range from $155.0 million to $215.0 million for the full year 2026, consisting of sustaining capital expenditures of approximately $105.0 to $115.0 million and discretionary capital expenditures of approximately $50.0 to $75.0 million for the final construction of Blue Creek.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed numbers demonstrate a large mismatch between the anchor-year sustaining expenditure and management's post-Blue Creek guidance. If the additional $43.7-$53.7 million is recurring and absent from the forecast, the base operating PV would be overstated by approximately $614-$754 million under the existing model's linear anchor relationship, a material change to intrinsic value and the buy-below level.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $168.6 million OE calculation, classify the 2026 capital program between recurring maintenance and finite completion spending, and rerun all scenarios using normalized sustaining capital without changing other assumptions.

audit_findings.title: The latest-actual anchor precedes Blue Creek's production step-change
audit_findings.mechanism: The valuation applies smooth growth to FY2025 OE even though Blue Creek's post-ramp volumes, costs, working capital and sustaining capital change the operating perimeter underlying the anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: Due to the accelerated startup of the longwall, we produced approximately 1.8 million metric tons in 2025 and expect to produce at a minimum approximately 4.1 to 4.4 million metric tons in 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter change is demonstrated: Blue Creek production was about 1.8 million metric tons in 2025 versus expected 2026 production of 4.1-4.4 million metric tons, and total company production reached 6.209 million metric tons in the first half of 2026. The monetary OE effect cannot be isolated from the supplied filings because realized prices, mine-level costs, working capital and normalized maintenance requirements are not separately bridged. The impact could materially raise or lower value.
audit_findings.action: Construct a post-ramp Blue Creek OE bridge using 2026 actual volumes, realizations, cash costs, taxes, working capital and normalized sustaining capital, then rerun the valuation from a comparable operating perimeter.

audit_findings.title: Mine-closure obligations may be an unmodeled senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $71.715 million at June 30, 2026, equal to $1.35 per diluted share and 2.66% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: If future reclamation cash settlements are absent from OE, the unrepresented ARO belongs in the equity bridge; deducting both modeled settlement cash flows and the liability would double count it.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025, we had recorded asset retirement obligation liabilities of $70.3 million, including $5.5 million reported as a current liability.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether an error exists remains unresolved because the record does not reconcile historical or forecast reclamation payments to OE. Even a conservative full deduction of the June 2026 current and long-term ARO would reduce base value only from $50.50 to about $49.15 per share and would not change the valuation conclusion relative to the $104.45 price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the ARO settlement schedule to reclamation cash payments retained in OE and deduct only the portion not already represented, with an explicit double-counting check.

audit_findings.title: Legacy black-lung liabilities require an explicit OE-to-bridge reconciliation
audit_findings.magnitude: $36.1 million at December 31, 2025, equal to $0.68 per diluted share and 1.34% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Legacy claim payments must either remain in normalized OE or be represented by a bridge deduction for the residual liability; omitting both overstates common-equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: Our estimated total black lung liabilities as of December 31, 2025 were $36.1 million (net of the black lung trust).
audit_findings.explanation: The liability is filed, but the modeling error remains unresolved because the supplied OE record does not show whether expected claim payments are retained. A full $36.1 million deduction would reduce base value to about $49.82 per share and would not change the conclusion relative to the market price. The related collateral must be handled consistently to avoid double counting.
audit_findings.action: Map expected legacy claim payments to each historical and forecast OE period, then either retain those outflows or deduct the uncovered liability while consistently treating the pledged collateral.

audit_findings.title: Collateral-backed short-term investments may have been added as excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $10.1 million, equal to $0.19 per diluted share and 0.38% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds all June 2026 cash and short-term investments, including investments pledged for black-lung claims that are not freely distributable to shareholders.
audit_findings.evidence: The short-term investments as of December 31, 2025 and December 31, 2024, consisted of $ 9.9 million and $ 9.5 million posted as collateral for the self-insured black lung related claims asserted by or on behalf of former employees of Walter Energy, Inc. ("Walter Energy") and its subsidiaries, which were assumed by the Company and relate to periods prior to March 31, 2016, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: This is demonstrated by the arithmetic: the $322.498 million bridge amount equals filed cash of $302.346 million plus gross short-term investments of $20.152 million, while the filing identifies $10.1 million of those investments as collateral. Removing it would reduce base value from $50.50 to about $50.31 per share, which is not material to the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Exclude $10.1 million from excess cash, or retain it only if the bridge also deducts the full associated black-lung claim liability; document the treatment to prevent double counting.
